FINDING 9 — `zen check` accepts a program whose emitted C does not compile; the
user gets a raw `cc` error, not a Zen diagnostic.

FILE: check_accepts_untyped_load_then_c_fails.zen.txt
        x: i32 := 5
        p := x.addr()
        println(load(offset(p, 0)))

CMD:  ./zen check tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/check_accepts_untyped_load_then_c_fails.zen.txt
OUT:  zenc: <file>: ok                                   rc 0

CMD:  ./zen run tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/check_accepts_untyped_load_then_c_fails.zen.txt
OUT:  /tmp/zenc_zd_NNNN.c: In function 'zen_main':
      /tmp/zenc_zd_NNNN.c:46: error: too many arguments to function 'println_void'
      rc 1

WHAT genc EMITS:
      println_void((*(((uint8_t*)(_z1__z1_p) + (0LL)))));
      `offset` reinterprets the typed `int32_t*` as `uint8_t*`, so `load` has no
      element type; the printer resolves to the no-Display fallback
      `println_void` (zero parameters) and is then handed an argument anyway.

CONTROL: `println(load(p))` — without the `offset` — checks AND runs fine
      (emits `println_i32((*p))`, prints 5).

CLASS: checker hole / checker-vs-emitter disagreement. Either `load` on an
      untyped pointer should be rejected with a Zen diagnostic, or the printer
      selection should fail loudly — leaking a C compiler error is neither.
FOUND BY: hand-directed probing of the intrinsic pointer surface (addr / store /
      load / offset), which tools/fuzz-diff.zen's grammar does not generate.
